$comment: P(lane | position of the seat within the enemy team), one row per seat in the order the client
lists them. Columns are top, jungle, mid, adc, support.
SHIPPED FLAT ON PURPOSE. Every row is 0.2, which means the seat index contributes nothing and
the prediction rests entirely on what the champion itself says about the lanes it plays.
Why: the original guess was that the client lists a team in canonical role order, so seat 2
would be mid and seat 3 adc. A recorded 5v5 tournament draft says otherwise — the client listed
the team as top, jungle, BOTTOM, MIDDLE, utility. Seats 0, 1 and 4 matched the guess; 2 and 3
That measurement is one sample from a custom game (isCustomGame=true, queueId=3110), where
positions are not handed out by matchmaking, so it does not settle what ranked solo/duo does.
It does settle that the canonical order cannot simply be assumed. And the ordering that actually
matters is the ENEMY team's, which the client never reveals — it can only be checked after a game
So: no hint until it is measured, rather than a hint that is known to be partly wrong.
To re-enable after measuring real ranked drafts, raise the diagonal — 0.36 with 0.16 elsewhere
is a mild nudge that cannot overrule the champion's own role distribution. Keep the rows summing
to 1; the loader normalises them anyway.
